title: ARIA roles need their required attributes
summary: An element has an ARIA role but is missing an attribute the role requires, such as aria-checked on a checkbox. Add the required attribute.
problem: An element has a role that requires certain ARIA attributes, and one is missing. For example, role="checkbox" requires aria-checked. Without it, assistive technology cannot report the state of the control.
whoItAffects: Screen reader users hear a role with no state, such as a checkbox that is neither checked nor unchecked. They cannot tell what they have chosen, and keyboard-only users depend on that same information.
steps: Find the element and the missing attribute in the scan result.
Look up the role in the WAI-ARIA specification to see which attributes it requires.
Add the attribute with its current value, and keep it in sync with the visual state in your script.
If you can, use a native control such as <input type="checkbox">, which exposes its state without ARIA.
whyItMatters: A control whose state is not exposed cannot be used with confidence, and people often get checkout or sign-in forms wrong because of it. This is a WCAG Level A requirement, the level that accessibility regulations and procurement requirements commonly build on.
howToCheck: Select the element in your browser's accessibility inspector and check that its state is shown. Toggle it and confirm the state changes.
